carbon_policy_signal.item: COP31 collapse weakens international fossil-fuel commitments; EU ETS auction outcomes on Wed–Thu will test whether carbon price holds above 30 EUR/tCO2 or slides on reduced regulatory pressure.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Failed climate accord reduces enforcement risk and near-term decarbonization urgency; weaker carbon floor supports coal marginal cost economics and pressures EUA into seasonal winter trough, lifting thermal dispatch.

freshness_caveat: Coal (8th-percentile) and clean_dark (48th-percentile) are stale as of 2025-12-26 and 2025-12-31 respectively (334 and 329 days old); latest live metrics (TTF, GB Power, DE Power, renewables, storage) are dated 2026-11-24 to 2026-11-25. All headline inferences draw on current market data where available.
risk_flags: Renewables at 21% of load (9th-percentile, −43% week-on-week) forces coal and gas to cover load; coal at 96 USD/t (8th-percentile) suggests limited downside cushion if wind recovers suddenly.
GB power 206.75 EUR/MWh (91st-percentile) vs DE 226.53 EUR/MWh (89th-percentile) — tight GB-DE spread narrows interconnect arbitrage; flows at risk if GB stability improves.

EU storage 68.4% full (17.7pp below 5-yr seasonal) — refill pace must accelerate into spring or H2 2027 winter will face structural tightness; TTF at 91.67 EUR/MWh (82nd-percentile) leaves limited upside headroom.
COP31 collapse and EU permitting relaxation create binary regulatory tail — EUA under pressure (38th-percentile, −6% week); near-term cliff risk if coal recall accelerates despite low carbon price.

base.summary: Renewables recover modestly; storage injection pace normalizes; thermal dispatch gradually eases as wind/solar mean-revert.

downside.summary: Wind output recovers sharply; mild weather eases heating load; US LNG supply glut depresses arbitrage; EUA stays sub-32 EUR/tCO2 — coal uncompetitive.

upside.summary: Renewable forecast worsens (wind cuts deepen); storage injection stalls; cold snap drives space-heating demand; EUA regulatory cliff triggers coal recall surge.

themes: GB power premium widens; interconnect risk
Storage deficit vs seasonal norm; winter refill concern
COP31 collapse weakens emissions regulation; coal/gas marginal cost support
top_drivers: Renewable scarcity (21% load, 9th-percentile): Coal and gas forced into merit order; low-carbon-price regime (38th-percentile EUA) reduces decarbonization incentive — coal at 8th-percentile offers minimal hedge value.

GB power premium (91st-percentile, 206.75 EUR/MWh): Tight GB-DE spread signals interconnect transmission stress; French nuclear or Benelux outages could widen further, but mean reversion risk if wind recovers.

Storage undershot seasonal (68.4%, −17.7pp): Refill pace must sustain >0.5% daily injection through spring; TTF at 82nd-percentile offers limited upside buffer if winter demand spike or supply shock materializes.
top_takeaway: Renewables at 9th-percentile crush merit order; GB power 91st-percentile signals tight interconnect; storage 17.7pp below seasonal average threatens H2 refill pace amid stalled climate policy.

watchlist.why: 9th-percentile call lifts thermal dispatch; 1–2 pp swing in renewable share moves DE power 5–8 EUR/MWh; monitor 10-day outlook for mean reversion risk.
91st-percentile GB premium signals interconnect transmission congestion; tactical spread trades possible if French nuclear or Benelux gen changes.
17.7pp below seasonal average; Nov–Dec injection rate will set Apr–May refinancing risk and spring power curve shape; below 0.5% daily inject triggers structural tightness signal.
US nat-gas storage 2% above 5-yr avg; sustained high US export availability may cap TTF upside; monitor Henry Hub and Singapore LNG spot for arbitrage widening.
COP31 collapse weakens near-term decarbonization pressure; coal support could accelerate if EUA falls below 30 EUR/tCO2; watch auctions Wed/Thu for supply reaction.
